decisions.mechanism: A sharp stone flake is held against a wooden handle and lashed in place with plant fibre, so the flake edge cuts while the stick gives grip.
decisions.chronologyExplanation: Flaked stone, sticks and plant cord all exist in the Origins era, before this item.

missingPrerequisites: a clay catalogue item (clay exists only as a processing state, so no plastic-body node is available)

decisions.mechanism: A pebble is rubbed between two coarser stones, so abrasion wears its surface smooth and rounded.
decisions.chronologyExplanation: Rubbing stone on stone needs nothing beyond stones, available from the start of Origins.

decisions.mechanism: Three lengths of plant fibre are twisted together so friction between them locks them into one stronger cord that can be closed into a loop.
decisions.chronologyExplanation: Plant fibre and strands exist in the Origins era.

decisions.mechanism: A bone is ground against coarse stone, which wears the bone away at one end until it narrows into a point.
decisions.chronologyExplanation: Bone and stone are primitives available from the start.

missingPrerequisites: a mold-capable item (e.g. a wooden brick frame) that exists before pottery in the catalogue

decisions.mechanism: A ground bone point is lashed to a wooden handle with plant fibre, giving a grip for piercing hide and fibre.
decisions.chronologyExplanation: Depends on the ground bone point from the same batch, plus sticks and strands from Origins.

missingPrerequisites: crucible or kiln able to melt copper
